summary: Genomic foundation models are increasingly used to propose DNA sequences and edits. But successful design requires capabilities that current benchmarks do not measure.
takeaways: Our benchmark reveals that genomic models now display signs of general utility but have yet to saturate on performance in even simple tasks.
Here we introduce BEND 2.0 (BENchmark for DNA language models), which tests how well models predict the effects of DNA changes and whether these predictions can guide sequence design.
Across eight tasks built on five experimental datasets, we find that model choice and how representations are accessed both affect performance.
